rationale: Four major patch findings: (1) the truncation indicator in WorkflowStateOutput renders as a no-op <Button> with no onClick, violating WCAG 4.1.2 — keyboard users can focus and activate it but nothing happens; (2) ChatAiMessage.tsx useEffect has no cancelled-flag cleanup, allowing stale .then() callbacks on unmount or rapid re-trigger; (3) WorkflowStateOutput.tsx useEffect likewise has no cancelled flag and no error handling on the inner async function, causing unhandled promise rejections on API error and a stale-state race on every poll; (4) the ContinueWithInputPopup test mock returns a plain string rather than the new { output, truncated, finish_reason } object, so result.output is undefined in tests and the updated caller is silently untested. All six acceptance criteria pass; no security, breaking-change, or public-API issues identified.

business_review.criterion: Drawer shows indicator when truncated: true; unchanged when false or absent.
business_review.notes: WorkflowStateOutput.tsx renders the warning Button only when truncated is truthy, renders null otherwise.

business_review.criterion: Chat view shows indicator when truncated: true; unchanged when false or absent.
business_review.notes: ChatAiMessage.tsx renders the warning div only when outputTruncated is truthy, renders null otherwise.

business_review.criterion: Indicator tooltip exposes raw finish_reason value on both surfaces.
business_review.notes: Both surfaces build the tooltip as `${TRUNCATION_TOOLTIP_PREFIX} (finish_reason: ${value})` when present, falling back to the bare prefix when absent.

business_review.criterion: WorkflowExecutionState type includes finish_reason and truncated.
business_review.notes: types/entity/workflow.ts adds finish_reason?: string | null and truncated?: boolean to WorkflowExecutionState.

business_review.criterion: getWorkflowExecutionStateOutput no longer discards finish_reason or truncated.
business_review.notes: Store method now returns the full WorkflowExecutionStateOutput object instead of only data.output.

business_review.criterion: All existing callers of getWorkflowExecutionStateOutput remain type-correct after the return type change.
business_review.notes: All three callers updated: WorkflowStateOutput uses result.output ?? '', WorkflowExecutionEditOutputForm returns result.output, ContinueWithInputPopup uses result.output.

standards_review.notes: Pre-commit hook enforces EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence pattern; hooks ran on all task commits without --no-verify.

Branch is EPMCDME-14145-workflow-truncation-indicator; convention requires underscore separator (EPMCDME-14145_workflow-truncation-indicator). Branch pre-dates this task and was not created by this diff — not blocking this review, but should be corrected before merge.

No dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Tooltip content rendered as text nodes (react-tooltip without html:true) — finish_reason value is safe even with angle brackets. No secrets, no open redirects, no new deps.
Valtio store pattern, optional-field typing, and useSnapshot usage follow existing codebase conventions.

findings.problem: WorkflowStateOutput.tsx renders the truncation indicator as a <Button> component with no onClick handler. The <button> element is focusable and activatable by keyboard, but activating it does nothing — violating WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
findings.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users encounter a focusable button that silently no-ops on activation. Screen readers announce it as an interactive button, misleading users who expect an action.
findings.recommendation: Replace the Button wrapper with a non-interactive tooltip anchor (a plain <span> or <div> styled to match the secondary button appearance) so the element is not in the tab order and not announced as interactive. Alternatively, add role="status" and aria-label describing the truncated state, removing the interactive semantics.

findings.problem: ChatAiMessage.tsx useEffect (lines 224–242) launches an async store call with no cleanup function. If the component unmounts or a dependency (stateId, executionId, workflow_id, isTerminalExecution) changes before the fetch resolves, the .then() callback still fires and calls setOutputTruncated / setOutputFinishReason on the detached or stale instance.
findings.impact: In a busy chat view where execution status flips or the user navigates away mid-fetch, stale callbacks overwrite correct state with out-of-order data. ContinueWithInputPopup already demonstrates the correct cancelled-flag pattern for this same store method.
findings.recommendation: Add a cancelled flag and cleanup: let cancelled = false; ...store.getWorkflowExecutionStateOutput(...).then((result) => { if (!cancelled) { setOutputTruncated(...); setOutputFinishReason(...) } }).catch(...); return () => { cancelled = true }.

findings.problem: WorkflowStateOutput.tsx getStateOutput async function (lines 53–67) has no cancelled flag and no try/catch. Concurrent fetches triggered by stateUpdatedDate, stateCompletedDate, or refreshKey changes race — the slower (older) fetch resolves last and resets output, truncated, and finishReason to stale values. Additionally, any API error (4xx/5xx from skipErrorHandling: true path) produces an unhandled promise rejection.
findings.impact: Under normal polling cadence, two in-flight requests can exist simultaneously; the one that launched first frequently resolves last (cold cache) and overwrites the most recent data. API errors on re-fetch produce unhandled rejections in production error monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the ContinueWithInputPopup pattern: add let cancelled = false, wrap the await in try/catch, gate all setState calls on !cancelled, and return () => { cancelled = true } from the effect.

findings.problem: The test mock in src/pages/workflows/details/states/__tests__/ContinueWithInputPopup.test.tsx (line 23) returns a plain string via .mockResolvedValue('Step output text'). After the return-type change, production code calls result.output on this value, yielding undefined. No test assertion checks for the text in the DOM, so the suite passes while silently testing broken behaviour.
findings.impact: The updated caller (result.output) is entirely untested. A regression that re-breaks result.output in ContinueWithInputPopup would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Update the mock to return the correct object shape: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ output: 'Step output text', truncated: false, finish_reason: null }). Add at least one test that asserts the output text renders in the popup body after the effect resolves.
